einzeiler: Former Green Beret Joe Kent discusses political betrayal, lobbying influence, and the…
kurzfassung: Joe Kent returns to the podcast to analyze the fallout from recent midterms and the widespread voter resentment caused by broken promises regarding foreign wars. He explains how pro-Israel lobbyists and special interest groups hijacked the administration's agenda, leading to economic strain and a massive loss of trust. Furthermore, Kent details his personal experiences with information gatekeeping in the White House and outlines what it will take for conservatives to rebuild credibility.
stichpunkte: Voters expressed deep betrayal during the midterms over the ongoing Iran war and soaring inflation.
Special interest groups and lobbyists heavily influenced key administration appointments and policy decisions.
Chief of staff Susie Wiles acted as a gatekeeper, shielding the president from dissenting intelligence.
The Iran war and regional instability severely damaged the credibility of the petrodollar system.
China strategically avoided escalating energy crises, positioning itself as a stabilizing economic mediator.
Intelligence figures like John Ratcliffe pushed mainstream narratives instead of challenging establishment policies.
Kent advocates for retracting American imperial overreach and focusing entirely on domestic self-reliance.
Political survival for the right requires abandoning neocon foreign policy and embracing true economic populism.
beschreibung:
Joe Kent is a retired U.S. Army Special Forces veteran, former CIA paramilitary officer, and former Director of the National Counterterrorism Center who resigned in March 2026 over his opposition to the Iran war. An Oregon native and Norwich University graduate in Strategic Defense Analysis, he served 20 years in the Army, completed 11 combat deployments, and earned six Bronze Stars before retiring in 2018 and joining the CIA’s Special Activities Center. His military service included assignments with the 75th Ranger Regiment, Army Special Forces, and U.S. Army Special Operations Command. In 2019, his wife, Navy Senior Chief Petty Officer Shannon Kent, was killed in a suicide bombing while serving in Syria.
